environment.notes: node_modules present; all dependencies resolve. No missing env vars block the suite. vitest.config.ts uses environment: node, globals: true.

failures.failure_message: Error: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/next/server' imported from .../node_modules/next-auth/lib/env.js. Did you mean to import "next/server.js"?
failures.root_cause_hypothesis: The suite imports @/middleware, which imports the real @/auth, which imports next-auth. Loading next-auth in Vitest's node environment triggers next-auth/lib/env.js -> next/server, which fails ESM resolution. Unlike the register/sign-in tests, middleware.test.ts does NOT mock @/auth, so the whole next-auth import chain is pulled in.
failures.suggested_fix_action: Add a vi.mock('@/auth', ...) at the top of middleware.test.ts that replaces the auth() HOC with an identity wrapper, e.g. mock auth so that auth(fn) returns fn. This both avoids the next-auth import chain and exposes the inner middleware function so the test can call it directly. Mirror the mocking pattern already used in register/__tests__/actions.test.ts, register/__tests__/page.test.ts, and sign-in/__tests__/page.test.ts.

failures.failure_message: tsc --noEmit exited 1. All errors are in src/middleware.__tests__/middleware.test.ts: TS2554 Expected 2 arguments, but got 1 (lines 10, 77); TS2339 Property 'status'/'headers' does not exist on type 'void | Response' (lines 13,14,16,80,83).
failures.root_cause_hypothesis: middleware.ts exports `auth(function middleware(req){...})` as default. The next-auth v5 auth() HOC types the exported handler as a NextAuthMiddleware requiring 2 args (req, ctx) and returning `void | Response`. The test calls middleware(request) with 1 arg and reads response.status/response.headers, which do not typecheck against `void | Response`. This is downstream of F1: the test treats the auth-wrapped handler as a plain (req) => Response function.
failures.suggested_fix_action: Fix is the same as F1. After mocking @/auth so auth(fn) returns the inner fn, the default export is the plain (req: NextRequest) => NextResponse function, which takes 1 arg and returns a NextResponse with .status/.headers. This resolves all TS2554/TS2339 errors and tsc --noEmit will pass. No production type changes needed.

failures.test_name: npm scripts > npm run format:check exits 0
failures.failure_message: AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0. prettier --check reports code style issues in 8 files.
failures.root_cause_hypothesis: Eight files are not Prettier-formatted: src/app/(auth)/register/actions.ts, src/app/(auth)/sign-in/actions.ts, src/app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx, src/app/api/me/route.ts, src/lib/auth/validation.ts, src/lib/repositories/user-repository.ts (coder-owned), and src/lib/repositories/__tests__/user-repository.test.ts, src/middleware.__tests__/middleware.test.ts (tester-owned). Purely a formatting drift, not a logic defect. Spans both coder and tester files.
failures.suggested_fix_action: Run `npm run format` (prettier --write .) once to reformat all 8 files, then re-run format:check. Because the affected files span both coder- and tester-owned files, a single repo-wide format pass by the orchestrator is the cleanest fix. Alternatively route the coder files to the coder and the two test files to the tester.

failures.test_name: npm scripts > npm run build exits 0 and produces .next/
failures.failure_message: next build failed: Module build failed: UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from "node:crypto" is not handled by plugins (Unhandled scheme). Import trace: node:crypto <- ./src/lib/repositories/user-repository.ts <- ./src/auth.ts
failures.root_cause_hypothesis: src/lib/repositories/user-repository.ts does `import crypto from "node:crypto"`. That module is pulled into src/auth.ts, which is imported by src/middleware.ts. Middleware is bundled for the Edge runtime, where webpack cannot resolve the `node:` URI scheme, breaking `next build`. The `node:crypto` import is the offending line.
failures.suggested_fix_action: Remove `import crypto from "node:crypto"` and call the global Web Crypto `crypto.randomUUID()` (available globally in Node 20+ (engines say >=20) and in the Edge runtime). This keeps InMemoryUserRepository.create's id generation identical while making the module Edge-bundle-safe. Do not introduce any other node: builtin imports into the auth/middleware import chain.

cross_cutting_notes: F1 and F2 share one root cause (missing @/auth mock in middleware.test.ts) and one fix resolves both.
F3 (formatting) and F4 (node:crypto build) are independent of the middleware test issue and can be fixed in parallel.
No spec_bug or env_bug found. The contract and impl-context are consistent with the observed failures; nothing requires a contract change.
